module: Customizable 'pretty' JSON encoder: sorts keys by weight (tableWeights), and lets a callback decide which tables are folded onto a single line and which are indented. Used to write readable configuration files (e.g. controls/bindings files).
usage:
local exampleTable = {control = 5, bindings = {{1,2}, {4,5,6,7}}}
local function foldingCallback(item, lvl, path)
  return path:sub(1,10) == '/bindings/' and tableSize(item) < 4
end
local tblWeights = {control = 10, bindings = 99} -- 1 = first, 99 = last, default 50
local json = require('jsonPrettyEncoderCustom').encode(exampleTable, nil, nil, tblWeights, foldingCallback)
notes: Without foldingCallback, fold is true: ALL tables are written on a single line ('{"a":1, ...}' / '[1, 2]'). To get indentation, the callback must return false for the table concerned.
The keys of tableWeights must be LOWERCASE (the code looks up weights[tostring(key):lower()]). Missing key = weight 50. At equal weight, sorting is by type then by value.
The path passed to the callback has the form '/key/subkey/3' (array indices included); lvl is the depth (1 for the root).

Arrays are detected by next(v) == 1 and next(v, #v) == nil (sequential array without holes). An empty array is written '{}'. NaN and infinities become 9e999 / -9e999. numberPrecision (if not nil) formats non-integers as %<n>.<n>f (the same integer n serves as width and precision) and integers as %d. vec3/quat (cdata) are written {"x":..,"y":..,"z":..[,"w":..]}. Other types (function, userdata) give null.

encode.desc: Encodes v to JSON text with keys sorted by weight and folding driven by foldingCallback. The last three arguments are optional; _levelPath is internal (recursion).

numberPrecision.desc: number of decimals for non-integers; nil = %.10g

tableWeights.desc: key sort weights (lowercase), default 50; a nil value causes an error in the sort because weights is indexed (provide at least {})

foldingCallback.type: fun(item: table, lvl: integer, path: string): boolean|nil
foldingCallback.desc: returns true to fold the table onto one line, false to indent it
